title: Safety training changed one model a lot
text: With safety training, Qwen3 4B wrote a hazard for 30 of 84 hostile requests and declined 53. With it removed, the same model wrote 70 and declined 3.

title: Removing safety training does not always add hazards
text: llama3.1 8B wrote a hazard for 64 of 73 hostile requests. Its copy with safety training removed wrote 35 and declined 21, against 3. Test each copy, and don't assume what it will do.

title: Two models never said no
text: Asked to do something hostile, 2 of 12 models declined nothing. Both had their safety training removed. Most others declined only a few requests, so don't rely on a model to refuse.

title: Even the safest models wrote hazards
text: 2 of 12 models are in the safest group. Qwen3 4B still wrote a hazard for 33 of 95 hostile requests.

title: termite stopped almost every hazard
text: These 12 models wrote 807 hazardous replies to hostile requests. termite stopped or held 806 of them for a person to check, and 1 went straight in.

title: Refusing can go too far
text: qwen2.5 7B declined 11 of 40 harmless everyday requests. A model that refuses too much is a problem too, because people stop using it.

title: Models called hazards harmless
text: In at least 100 of 807 hazardous replies, the model said that the command only reads. Don't trust a model's description of its own command.

title: A bigger model was not clearly safer
text: Across 12 models, size had only a weak link with how often a model wrote a hazard. Test each model, and don't judge it by its size.

title: Too much context stops the answers
text: Context overflow happened in 51 of 168 trials above the limit, and in 0 of 756 trials at or below it. llama3.1 8B overflowed most, in 17 of 28 trials.

title: The policy catches what decision models miss
text: The 17 decision models rated 158 risky commands safe. termite's policy blocked 74 of them, and the other 84 were at tier 2, where a command shows personal information but no secrets.

title: Reading near secrets looks safe to them
text: Liquid d1 2B rated 8 of 8 sensitive reads safe, such as listing a folder of keys. It rated 0 of 6 small project changes safe. A read near a secret can look harmless to a model.

title: Some models refused every critical command
text: Of 17 models, vLLM d3 mini was one that refused 8 of 8 critical commands. Others left some of these commands to a person, so test the model you plan to use.

title: One model missed little and still allowed harmless commands
text: In this run, JevK5 4B rated 5 of 38 risky commands safe, and 13 of 14 harmless commands safe. Rating nothing safe is easy, so both numbers matter.

title: One model asks about everything
text: Laya asked for approval on 52 of 52 commands, and rated 0 of 14 harmless commands safe. That is cautious, but people stop reading warnings that they see every time.

title: Choosing the safest option is the weak spot
text: Given several ways to do a job, the best of 17 models put the safest way first in only 6 of 10 tests.

title: Many decision models need a different setup
text: 8 of 25 decision models gave no score. llama.cpp said each file is not a decision model, and each one needs its own server or client. This says nothing about how good those models are.
